svg.text: The knowledge base: 387 upstream pull requests, distilled by hand
It ships inside the app, so the phone can search it with no network at all — which is the point: the phone usually cannot reach GitHub.
the source
387 pull requests across the two
upstream projects: the failures they
fixed, the evidence that named them,
and the layer each fix belongs to
read, sorted and written down by hand
five documents and an index
build-failures.md — the build that stops at a stage
shader-split.md — the split that finds too few shaders
runtime-symptoms.md — crash, black screen, garble, freeze
device-findings.md — what it looks like on a phone, the first
move, and the dead ends that were ruled out
porting-method.md — how to measure a title, read a crash
report, and where a fix belongs
case-index.tsv — every case, one row, searchable
scripts/kb_search.py — the search itself
each case says: the symptom, the causes in order, what
tells them apart, which layer owns the fix, and whether
this fork already has it
The knowledge base is written by a person, on a computer.
The player's own cases are the other half: they live on the
phone, and they are found by the same search.
a question, answered offline
"the screen stays black after the intro movie"
→ the host drives one audio renderer, and this game opens
a second one for its movies: its event never fires, the
game waits inside the movie, the scene stops drawing
→ the evidence: 131 draws per frame became 2, and the log
says a second renderer was refused
→ the fix belongs to the engine, not to this game's profile
→ the case is in the index; the upstream has one too
no network was used for any of it
why this is the interesting part
This knowledge was never rare — it was scattered across
hundreds of pull requests, and it stayed there.
Bringing a game up meant reading the crash, finding the
layer and writing the fix: an evening per game, per
person, and only for the people who could do that.
Now it is on every phone that installs the app.
what it costs, and what it asks of you
The knowledge base is a set of text files in the app. It is not a model, it does not run on your phone, and it costs nothing.
The model is yours: the app asks for a provider, a model and a key, and the key stays on the phone. A cheap model is enough for most cases.
Adding to it is a normal pull request: one document, one case row, one sentence about the evidence. The maintainer reads it the way every other fix is read.
The upstream's pull requests are the source; a case that is not in the index yet is a case the next phone cannot find. That is the whole contribution loop.
